wedge: party size + route preset + car efficiency/fuel + toll/parking + station/terminal access + rail/bus fares => show the household-specific crossover point where car vs KTX/bus becomes cheaper; focus on the decision boundary rather than generic route/fare lookup
last_material_result: Distribution/data-gap validation found real search intent around car-vs-KTX/bus cost comparisons for Seoul-Busan, Seoul-Gangneung and Seoul-Jeonju archetypes, but also found a meaningful substitute: CalKit already publishes a 2026 Seoul-Busan/major-route comparison with KTX/SRT/bus and car costs split by party size. This weakens a generic total-cost comparison. The surviving wedge is narrower: an interactive household-specific crossover calculator including first/last-mile and parking, because current search results remain mostly static articles/tables. Exact live routing is unnecessary for an MVP: route presets plus editable distance, fuel efficiency, fuel price, toll, parking and access-cost assumptions can keep the product standalone and zero-API. Toll and rail/bus fares can be maintained as small preset tables with user override. This materially reduces platform-dependence risk but raises SEO differentiation risk because static comparison content is already abundant.
economics: KRW0 validation spend. Monetization remains ads plus travel/parking/rental-car affiliate or portfolio cross-promotion; no subscription thesis. A viable micro-asset likely needs long-tail route/party-size SEO rather than one generic calculator page. Revenue is still unproven and expected contribution remains KRW10k-50k/month only if organic acquisition is cheap and maintenance stays preset-based.
next_checkpoint: Next run: test three materially different distribution wedges before BUILD consideration: (1) route-specific crossover pages such as '서울 부산 3명 차 vs KTX', (2) holiday/family-trip variant including toll exemptions/parking, and (3) destination-day-trip variant where local mobility makes bringing a car more valuable. Look for evidence that these queries/results are not already saturated by calculators. KILL if all three are dominated by static publishers/calculators or require live paid routing data to be useful.
recommendation: KEEP for one more bounded validation round, but narrow from generic door-to-door comparator to party-size crossover decision. Do not BUILD yet; competition is now a material risk and three distribution wedges must survive first.
